name: Can I build a garage conversion ADU on a narrow lot or small backyard?

mainEntity.name: If my lot is small, can the existing garage still become a legal ADU without setback or access problems?
mainEntity.text: If my lot is small, can the existing garage still become a legal ADU without setback or access problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Small lots can be challenging, but they are not automatically disqualified. The existing garage footprint may already be in a buildable location, which makes conversion more feasible than new construction. The real issue is whether the existing structure can be adapted without violating setbacks, access paths, drainage needs, or minimum living standards. Narrow sites also make construction logistics harder, especially if materials, equipment, and utility work must pass through tight side yards. A lot that looks too small for a detached ADU may still be perfect for a conversion because the shell already exists. Homeowners should request a site feasibility review that looks at the garage location, property lines, roof condition, and utility access. That early analysis helps avoid expensive redesigns and clarifies whether the project should be a full conversion, partial conversion, or another type of ADU.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, a small lot can still work if the existing garage already fits within allowable dimensions and access rules. The key issues are setbacks, fire access, utility routes, and whether the converted structure can meet habitable space requirements without enlarging the footprint.
